name: NC-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +17 partisan lean
Incumbent Deborah Ross running with a large cash advantage
Republican challenger has reported no fundraising
Prediction markets price Ross at 99% to win
model.rationale: The district's +17 Democratic lean, Ross's incumbency and roughly $1.3 million war chest against a Republican opponent with no reported fundraising all point to a decisive Democratic win, and markets agree at 99%. No polls or expert ratings exist, but the fundamentals leave little room for doubt.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Ross or an unexpectedly strong Republican fundraising effort would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Deborah Ross, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Raleigh-area district that leans Democratic by about 17 points. She enters the general election with roughly $1.3 million in cash after raising about $1.7 million, while her Republican opponent, Eugene Douglass, has reported no fundraising. A Libertarian is also on the ballot but has shown no measurable campaign activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Ross about a 99% chance of winning. The combination of a favorable district, incumbency, and a large financial edge makes this one of the safest Democratic House seats up this cycle, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
